key_insight: An exact average-atom potential can be derived directly from a linear atomic cluster expansion and used to recover disordered-alloy properties without relying on an averaged parent potential.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable, data-efficient screening of chemically disordered alloys for structural, elastic, and thermodynamic behavior using small training sets.
method: Fit a linear ACE to Fe-W data from an EAM potential, then derive the average-atom potential and compare against explicit random-supercell and conventional averaged models.
Fit a linear ACE to ~1500 DFT Mo-Nb structures (~7 atoms each) and evaluate the resulting average-atom potential on key alloy properties.
Compare chemical site bases and assess transferability for elastic constants, lattice parameter, mixing enthalpy, Bain path, and surface energies.
evidence_signal: The Mo-Nb model trained on about 1500 small DFT structures reproduced DFT elastic constants, lattice parameter, mixing enthalpy, Bain path, and, with the occupation basis, surface energies.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the chosen chemical site basis, so an unsuitable basis may miss important properties such as surface energies.
paper_title: Benchmarking average atom potentials derived from atomic cluster expansions
